Basis for Intervening:
The Citizens Utility Board of Wisconsin (“Wisconsin CUB”) moves to intervene in this matter pursuant to Rule 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.214. Wisconsin CUB has an interest that will be directly affected by the outcome of this proceeding. 

Wisconsin CUB is designated by Wisconsin law to advocate on behalf of residential and small business energy utility customers. The Wisconsin Legislature intended CUB to, among other things, represent the rights of customers before regulatory agencies. See Wis. Stat. §§ 196.315, 199.02. Wisconsin CUB advocates for its members and for all residential and small business public utility customers of the state. 

Wisconsin CUB has an interest in ensuring that Wisconsin residential and small business customers receive affordable and reliable electricity service.  The proposed tariff changes are intended to address challenges to the reliability of the grid created by large load customers in MISO, including in Wisconsin, and may also impact the rates paid by Wisconsin’s residential and small business customers. As the sole entity designated by Wisconsin law to advocate for Wisconsin consumers, no other party adequately represents the interests of Wisconsin CUB, and its participation in this matter is in the public interest. 

Wisconsin CUB thus requests that the Commission grant this motion to intervene.
